references.text: The Gadites and Reubenites confirm that they will cross the Jordan armed, which contrasts with the consequence described in verse 30 if they do not.
Moses describes the positive outcome if the tribes cross the Jordan armed, which is the condition to which verse 30 offers an alternative.
Describes the land of Canaan as the inheritance that the children of Israel are to receive, the same land mentioned in verse 30 as an alternative settlement place.
Joshua offers the tribes east of the Jordan the opportunity to have property in the land of Canaan if their own inheritance is unclean, a similar idea about settling in Canaan.
Uses the same expression 'וְנֹאחֲזוּ' (and they took possession) regarding Israel who settled in Egypt, parallel to the concept of property in Canaan.
